card.summary: Web Folder Basic: 'No capacity limit. Auto-deleted 90 hours after upload.' API flow: 10 files per WebFolder, 999 GiB max per file

free_tier.stated: Web Folder Basic: 'No capacity limit. Auto-deleted 90 hours after upload.' API flow: 10 files per WebFolder, 999 GiB max per file

retention.stated: Auto-deleted 90 hours after upload.' API flow: 10 files per WebFolder, 999 GiB max per file

egress.terms: No egress charge; instead a hard time gate. Free download window is 48 h (<10 GB), 12 h (10-20 GB), 6 h (>=20 GB); after that a $2+ Download Pass or $5 expiry extension is required.

record.tooling: Documented v2 REST API at api.file.kiwi (POST /v2/folders returns presigned R2 PUT URLs), 36 h presigned-URL validity, client-side E2E keys (RFC 8188 AES-128-GCM); no rclone backend
record.chaining: No account at all. One API call creates a folder; anonymous IDs are unlimited. Multiplication is trivial, the 90-hour delete is the wall.
record.limits_note: 999 GiB/file; 10 files/WebFolder; 90 h total life; download window collapses to 6 h for >=20 GB; 1 concurrent chunk upload; download count capped at 3 in Korea
record.reliability_note: 6-48 h download windows make it a transfer tool, not storage; the 90 h auto-delete is unconditional

evidence.proved: 'Web Folder Basic — No capacity limit. Auto-deleted 90 hours after upload. $0'; lifecycle T0 -> T0+6~48 h -> T0+90 h

Limits table: 'Files per WebFolder 10 · Max file size 999 GiB · Presigned URL validity 36 hours · Download count (Korea) 3'; 'Free Download Hours by File Size: <10 GB 24 hours / 10-20 GB 12 hours / >=20 GB 6 hours'

card.summary: Prepaid Upload-GB: 50 GB upload $1.20, 100 GB $1.60, 500 GB $3.99, 1000×n GB $6.99×n. 1 Upload-GB = a 1 GB file kept available for 7 days.

free_tier.stated: Prepaid Upload-GB: 50 GB upload $1.20, 100 GB $1.60, 500 GB $3.99, 1000×n GB $6.99×n. 1 Upload-GB = a 1 GB file kept available for 7 days.

retention.stated: 1 Upload-GB = a 1 GB file kept available for 7 days

egress.terms: Downloads are gated per-file, not metered: 'download requires a Download Pass or Expiry Postponement'. One-time Download Pass $2.00 (≤5 GB) or $2.00 + $0.40/GB above 5 GB. File Expiration Extension $5.00 buys 6 more hours, repeatable.

record.limits_note: 90-hour hard auto-delete on the free folder; 7-day default lifetime on paid folders; expiry purchased in 6-hour or 7-day increments
record.reliability_note: This is a TRANSFER service priced per upload-with-a-deadline, not storage. The '1000 GB for $6.99' line is a one-shot: 1 TB uploaded and held for 7 days. Annualised storage-equivalent is astronomically worse.

evidence.proved: '50 GB upload $1.20 · 100 GB upload $1.60 · 500 GB upload $3.99 · 1000 × n GB upload $6.99 × n'; '1 Upload-GB lets you upload a 1 GB file and keep it available for 7 days'; 'One-time Download Pass $2.00 … ≤ 5 GB: $2.00 · > 5 GB: + $0.40/GB'; 'File Expiration Extension $5.00 … Each purchase adds 6 hours'
(free tier) — 'Web Folder Basic … No capacity limit. Auto-deleted 90 hours after upload'

record.price_per_tb_month: $6.99 per TB for a 7-day hold = $6.99 × (30.4/7) ≈ $30.36/TB/mo to hold 1 TB continuously. To hold 20 TB: ~$607/mo. Roughly 30× the 1fichier/Blomp floor. Dead end for storage; only rational as a paid download-enabler for a one-off link.
